notes: This release is about seeing the migration whole. The new Content Flow diagram (Sitemap toolbar → Content Flow) shows where your content is now on the left, where it ends up on the right, and sizes every band by how many pages it carries. Three readings you switch between inside the view: straight onto the Keep/Kill/Evolve/Consolidate/Exclude decisions, straight onto the new sitemap's sections, or both at once with the decisions as the middle column — that last one is usually what you want in front of a client, because it makes plain that you're not just moving pages, you're deciding about them. Any decision states you've added yourself get their own block in the color you gave them, and pages nobody has reviewed collect in an "(unreviewed)" block, so the diagram doubles as a picture of how far the audit has got. Crucially it also shows the content that arrives nowhere — Retired, Out of scope, and Not yet placed — which on most audits is the biggest number on the page. Consolidated pages flow through to wherever their master page lands, since the URL dies but the content survives. If you're merging several sites into one, the left column can be the source site instead of the section, which is usually the real question: which site is contributing what, and where does it land. Source sites start out named after their web address, so the setup dialog offers to give them proper names first. Export HTML hands a client the whole thing — every reading, in any browser, with no app.
